summary: Karen O'Brien-Kop works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London, where she was a senior teaching fellow, before holding lecturer posts at Roehampton (attested 2020) and King's College London (2022).

Karin Meyers specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy, having studied under Jay L. Garfield. She served as assistant professor and MA program director at Kathmandu University's Centre for Buddhist Studies at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Karin Preisendanz is an Indologist and philosopher who earned her doctorate and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg. Her career includes posts at FU Berlin, the University of British Columbia, Hamburg, and as professor at the University of Vienna (1999).

Karl Albert Agathon Benary studied at Göttingen, Halle-Wittenberg (doctorate), and under Franz Bopp in Berlin. A linguist, he served as Gymnasiallehrer at Cöllnisches Gymnasium (1833–1860) and Privatdozent at Humboldt University of Berlin (1839).

Karl Ammer studied at Vienna under Bernhard Geiger, Erich Frauwallner, Nikolai Trubetzkoy, and Wilhelm Havers, receiving his PhD. A linguist and Indologist, he worked at Vienna (1938–1954) before serving as professor and institute director at Halle-Wittenberg (1954–1970).

Karl Benedikt Hase studied at Jena, Helmstedt, and under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. A linguist and historian, he held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, École des langues orientales vivantes, École Polytechnique, and the University of Paris.

Karl Bernhard Seidenstücker studied at Göttingen, Halle, and Leipzig, earning his PhD under Ernst Windisch. Active in Buddhist studies and Indology, he held posts at the Maha Bodhi Society and the Museum am Rothenbaum (1916).

Karl Bohnenberger, a linguist, earned his PhD at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and Eduard Sievers. He spent his career at Tübingen as librarian (1888–1921), Privatdozent (1892), ao. Professor (1899), and ord. Professor (1921–1930).

Karl Brugmann studied at Halle, Bonn, and Leipzig, completing his PhD under Georg Curtius. A specialist in linguistics and Indology, he taught at Alte Nikolaischule, the University of Freiburg, and the University of Leipzig (1877–1919).

Karl Brunnhölzl is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who received his training under traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Tenga Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Khenpo Lama Thubten.

Karl Debreczeny works in Tibetology and art history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago under Hung Wu and Jenny Purtle, and served as curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (attested 2008).
Karl Dyroff, who studied at Kronberg Gymnasium Aschaffenburg, worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He held an academic post at the University of Munich from around 1903 to 1934.

Karl Eduard Zachariae von Lingenthal studied at Sankt Afra zu Meißen, Leipzig, Berlin, and Heidelberg. Working in history and related fields, he held a post at Heidelberg University from around 1836 to 1842.

Karl Eugen Neumann worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Berlin and Halle, and earned his PhD at Leipzig under Richard Pischel, having also studied under Ernst Windisch, Paul Deussen, Albrecht Weber, and Hermann Oldenberg.
Karl Felix Halm was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. From approximately 1856 to 1882, he held dual posts at the University of Munich and the Bavarian State Library.

Karl Ferdinand Johansson, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Uppsala University under Olof August Danielsson and Per Persson. He spent his career at Uppsala as Privatdozent (1886), acting professor (1889–1890), and professor (1893; 1908–1925).

Karl Florenz earned his PhD at Leipzig under Ernst Windisch and studied under Max Müller. A scholar of Japanology, Indology, and linguistics, he taught at the University of Tokyo (1889–1917) and the Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut/University of Hamburg (1914–1935).

Karl Friedrich Burkhard studied at Munich, Erlangen, and Halle (PhD), studying under August Friedrich Pott and Emil Rödiger. A linguist and Indologist, he taught at Evangelisches Gymnasium Teschen and Akademisches Gymnasium Wien, and directed Franz-Joseph-Gymnasium Wien (1874–1890).

Karl Friedrich Geldner completed his PhD at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. A scholar of Indology and Iranian studies, he taught at Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, Humboldt University of Berlin (from 1890), and as professor at Marburg (1907–1921).

Karl Friedrich Hermann studied at Heidelberg under Friedrich Creuzer and at Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann. A scholar of history and archaeology, he held academic positions at Heidelberg University (~1826–1832), Marburg (~1832–1842), and Göttingen (~1842–1855).
